approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from real observations. It breeds from score-ranked groups of a greedy survivor population, uses its existing fragment crossover and local graph edits to build a fresh pool, and rejects invalid or previously evaluated identities. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange route is disabled. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive using count fingerprints and a count-sensitive Tanimoto covariance. It draws correlated score functions over the pool and evaluates one still-available maximizer from each function. Real feedback then updates the archive, predictor, survivors and future breeders.
approach.novelty: Reserve only the final successful batch choice for the molecule with the greatest posterior variance remaining after accounting for the locations of the preceding choices and the inherited observation noise. Every preceding Thompson choice uses exactly the original draw and mask. This tests whether one deliberately information-seeking evaluation supplies useful later feedback. Earlier siblings removed sampled residuals or their correlation, froze later model learning, or optimized sampled immediate batch improvement; none establishes the value of this final variance choice. The older all-position conditioning experiment changed later random functions by assuming pending scores equaled their means. This proposal changes one acquisition objective, without assigning any score to a pending molecule.

hypothesis: Replace only the final successful posterior-selection position by the smallest-index maximizer of the original latent posterior variance conditional on earlier selected locations with the inherited observation noise, while preserving every preceding masked correlated Thompson choice and learning only from real accepted feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-seeking labels changed predictions but never bred, and mean final score fell by 0.02279
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and heterocyclic families coexist with tiny fragments, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-062b351ccb52 produces substituted indole/azaindole amides, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-alkyl and cyclic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen-carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl frameworks. All supplied Child and accepted published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory paths were present and read: each task has 900 observations across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 accepted optimizer proposals. No task is omitted and no comparison path is missing. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. The present comparison is therefore a complete matched chemistry comparison under the supplied Research in Depth profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task. The published n-62daf219c70a report records exact reproduction of its same-code source n-c55c3d520a2c; its own historical profile mismatch is not a missing pairing for this Child. The original gaps below retain that source history, rather than treating the baseline reproduction as an independent chemical discovery. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9 to 0.9138 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8552 to 0.8977. These are molecule-level incidences of SMILES text features, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task. A read-only CPU RDKit pass over the supplied trajectories supplies the explicitly labelled heavy-atom, bond and ring readings below; all accepted optimizer records parsed. Perceived cycles follow a graph ring-perception convention, not independent ring systems or proof of accessible three-dimensional geometry. The global aromatic abundance does not describe every leader: the leading seed-0 fluorinated imino/carbonyl molecule has no perceived aromatic atoms. Neutral strings also do not imply an absence of basic amines, and absent stereomarkers do not imply an absence of potentially stereogenic centres. The Child contains 382 accepted optimizer proposals with at most five heavy atoms, versus 123 in the Parent, with the Child count higher in every matched seed/task pair. These counts describe evaluated outputs; they do not identify which generator or acquisition component caused them. Rich ring chemistry coexists with N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide and unconventional sulfur environments, strained-looking ring closures, and unspecified stereochemistry. Ordinary aryl fluorides, amines, amides and heterocycles also occur, so synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly impossible. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with much narrower families among nearby high-scoring records. Perceived graph differences, SMILES uniqueness and ring presence are not founder ancestry: no founder count, independent lineage count, component attribution or causal diversity benefit is inferred here. Scores quoted below are observed trajectory values, not new scores or measurements of synthesis, stability or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's retained best molecule. Reproducible descriptor observations and source hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot1-molecular/chemistry_observations.json; this audit path is documentation, not authority for SMILES citations. Citations come only from the digest and request-granted Child trajectories. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-seeking labels changed predictions but never bred, and mean final score fell by 0.02279
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-seeking labels changed predictions but never bred, and mean final score fell by 0.02279
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.
